title: Commissioning Engineer
description:
TerraPower is a nuclear technology company based in Bellevue, Washington. At its core, the company is working to raise living standards globally through a more affordable, secure, and environmentally friendly form of nuclear energy along with innovations in medical isotopes to improve human health. In 2006, TerraPower originated with Bill Gates and a group of like-minded visionaries who evaluated the fundamental challenges to raising living standards around the world. They recognized energy access was crucial to the health and economic well-being of communities and decided that the private sector needed to take action and create energy sources that would advance global energy deployment. TerraPower’s mission is to be a world leader in new nuclear technologies, while developing innovators and future leaders in the nuclear field. As a result, the company’s activities in the fields of nuclear energy and related sciences are yielding significant innovations in the safety and economics of nuclear power, hybrid energy and medical applications – all for significant human health benefits.”

TerraPower is seeking to hire highly motivated and forward-thinking professionals who are interested in focusing on advanced nuclear reactor research and development and influencing change within the nuclear power landscape and bringing forward the critical production of medical isotopes. TerraPower is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Commissioning Engineer III

The Commissioning Engineer III reports to the USO Commissioning Manager and is focused on the integrated design, commissioning, and operation of plant systems, structures and integrated analysis of the facility with a focus on Commissioning plan and product development. This Commissioning Engineer III position requires a high potential individual who will focus on nuclear island commissioning and plant operations related aspects of the Natrium Demonstration Plant being developed including scheduling, planning, and testing product development. The successful candidate will coordinate with engineers and project management professionals working on systems, components, engineering analysis, test planning, and scheduling in areas such as plant design, plant commissioning, and execution schedule development. The Commissioning Engineer III will work as part of a high-performing team of engineers, operators, and project managers.

Responsibilities

  • Responsible for coordinating geographically diverse design and commissioning team members to develop supporting design and testing documentation. The team is composed of TerraPower employees, subcontracted resources, partner employees, and customers.
  • Develop and implement commissioning administrative programs and
  • Develop and coordinate the creation of an integrated nuclear plant commissioning schedule across multiple organizations.
  • Provide subject matter expertise to the project team regarding regulations, company policies, and industry best practices related to nuclear plant commissioning.Support the develop, maintenance, and refinement of plant level and system level requirements, specifications, and strategy documents related to commissioning, plant operations and maintenance activities over the lifecycle of a nuclear facility
  • Apply Engineering principles, methods, and tools to the design of nuclear and industrial facilities and its systems and operations.
  • Develop and lead commissioning and design efforts to evaluate plant integrated control and transient event responses and provide recommendations/optimizations to deliver efficient plant operational strategies to influence design.
  • Support teammates and contractors in the plant development efforts through oversight and interface activities.
  • Support continuous learning and application of nuclear industry best practices to maintain the highest quality of engineering design and proactively identify process change/enhancement opportunities.
  • Support licensing activities associated with Safety Analysis
  • Provide leadership and oversight of nuclear island commissioning programs, processes, and procedures to ensure testing meets design criteria.

Key Qualifications and Skills

  • B.S. degree in Nuclear, Mechanical, Electrical, or other relevant engineering discipline from an accredited university or equivalent experience
  • 7+ years direct nuclear power plant experience commissioning safety-related (or equivalent) systems and components
  • 5+ years direct experience in commercial nuclear reactor operating experience, including Senior Reactor Operator qualification or equivalent; Shift Technical Advisor qualification preferred
  • Experience in developing and/or using nuclear plant commissioning administrative processes and procedures
  • Experience in implementing integrated plant design of nuclear systems, including complex systems and structures highly desired but not required
  • Experience developing and/or approving nuclear plant operations and maintenance procedures is preferred
  • Experience using P6 Primavera or a similar application to develop long-term schedules is preferred.
  • Knowledge of the implementing requirements for and licensing basis criteria for nuclear work control, maintenance strategies, and operational programs
  • Deep understanding of the nuclear regulations, plant work control processes, operational design philosophies, and integrated plant operations during normal and off-normal events
  • Deep understanding of configuration management principles, as well as knowledge of design control tools application on nuclear or similar complex industrial applications
  • Knowledge of Risk Informed methodologies for integrated plant design or similar probabilistic methods in design, desired but not required
  • Excellent technical writing, communication, and presentation skills, including periodic training development and presentation
  • Attention to detail and aspiration for technical
  • Candidate must be a high potential, self-starter and possess ability to coordinate and support a design team’s effort with minimal direction
  • Ability to handle projects that include many competing objectives and design constraints, with ability to resolve conflicts between objectives
  • Ability to work on tasks that require a multi-disciplinary
  • Experience working to quality standards NQA-1 or ISO
  • The successful candidate will possess a high degree of trust and integrity, communicate openly and display respect and a desire to foster teamwork

  • Motor Abilities: Sitting for extended periods, bending/stooping, grasping/gripping, fine motor control (hands)

CAP implementation Specialist

The CAP implementation specialist reports directly to the Procedure Manager and will fill one or more of the following roles to support the Natrium Demonstration Project (NDP) based on qualifications and experience. The Corrective Action Specialist is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the Kemmerer Power Station (KPS) Corrective Action Program including analyzing corrective action data and utilizing the data to understand causes for quality, safety, and business process impacts. The ideal candidate will have experience in issue identification, resolution, categorization, cause analysis, preventive action, and trend analysis. The successful candidate will integrate and coordinate with other departments, project partners, regulators, and outside organizations working on procedure development.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute a plan for configuring and implementing the Kemmerer Power Station (KPS) CAP software.
  • Develop and maintain processes and standards for the KPS corrective action program
  • Coordinate with other departments for cross-discipline support of software and CAP development
  • Use smart procedures or other software-based support tools to develop and maintain the Corrective Action Program
  • Consider and integrate use of cross-trained resources in Software development to improve organizational efficiency.
  • Identify existing industry guidance for processes that can be adopted with minimal modifications to meet KPS goals
  • Use industry practices to develop high-quality procedures which minimize risk of safety or human performance events.
  • Engage with industry peers, 3rd party vendors, NEI, EPRI, and other organizations to find innovative methods and technologies for developing and using software and AI in the Corrective Action Program.
  • Ensure Corrective Action Program in Software complies with company standards, NRC regulations, and other codes, standards, and regulatory requirements.
  • Maintains the Corrective Action Program by monitoring, tracking and identifying trends for corrective action data to provide performance improvements.
  • Develops and maintains status reports as directed.
  • Facilitate CAP/PI screening committee meetings.
  • Coordinate and participate in self-assessments, critiques, and benchmarking activities.
  • Manage and maintain the operating experience program
  • Monitor and maintain the site performance indicators

Discipline-Specific Education and Experience

  • 5+ years’ experience in working in the development and management of software based corrective action program with at least 3 years’ experience specific to Software
  • 5+ years’ experience with implementing or using a Nuclear Corrective Action Program

Key Qualifications and Skills

  • High level of knowledge of nuclear power plant systems and terminology.
  • Prior experience in Corrective Action programs
  • Experience with interpreting relevant nuclear information and standards in strict procedural and regulatory compliance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience with smart procedures or other software-based procedure tools.
  • Excellent technical writing and communication skills.
  • Attention to detail and aspiration for procedural excellence.
  • Self-starter who can develop innovative solutions with minimal supervision.
  • Cause analysis training and/or certification
  • The successful candidate will:

- possess a high degree of trust and integrity, openly communicate, and display respect and a desire to foster teamwork.

Data Architect

TerraPower is searching for an experienced Data Architect to lead the design, governance, and standards of our enterprise data ecosystem. Our organization continues to add applications and data and we are looking to design and implement a scalable, governed data infrastructure, potentially centered around a unified Data Hub strategy to accelerate AI-training readiness, and to provide frictionless data-sharing and data interoperability. This role will establish the policies, patterns, and platforms that enable confident decision-making across the business.

The role will work hands-on within our Azure-centric stack, primarily Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse Analytics, while partnering closely with Data Engineers, Application, Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity resources. This is a high-impact, cross-functional role with visibility across the entire organization.

Key Responsibilities

Data Governance & Standards

  • Establish and champion enterprise-wide data governance policies, standards, and best practices for data creation, storage, access, quality, and lifecycle management
  • Define and maintain a data catalog, data dictionary, and metadata management framework
  • Develop and enforce data classification standards in collaboration with Legal and Cybersecurity to ensure appropriate handling of sensitive and regulated data
  • Create and own data modeling standards (conceptual, logical, and physical) across all platforms

Create and own data quality and process monitoring frameworks to ensure the health, reliability, and lineage of data across the enterprise.Architecture & Design

  • Design and evolve the enterprise data lake into a data lakehouse architecture, ensuring it supports current workloads and scales to accommodate future application acquisitions and integrations
  • Lead the architectural design of data ingestion, transformation, and storage patterns within Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse Analytics
  • Define reference architectures and design patterns for data integration, ensuring new applications and data sources are onboarded consistently and securely
  • Evaluate and recommend tools, frameworks, and emerging technologies to continuously improve the data platform
  • Evaluate a Data Hub architecture to streamline the exchange of data between operational applications and the analytical lakehouse, reducing point-to-point integration complexity

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with the Infrastructure Architect to align data platform design with infrastructure, networking, and cloud resource management strategies
  • Work with Cybersecurity to implement data access controls, encryption standards, auditing, and compliance requirements
  • Guide and mentor a team of Data Engineers, providing technical leadership, reviewing designs, and ensuring adherence to architectural standards
  • Collaborate with project teams and business stakeholders across multiple concurrent projects to define data requirements and integration approaches for new and acquired applications

Project & Integration Support

  • Serve as the data architecture lead across multiple simultaneous projects, providing guidance from initiation through deployment.
  • Define repeatable integration patterns for acquired applications being onboarded into the company data lake, including data mapping, transformation logic, and quality validation.
  • Document architecture decisions, data flows, and integration specifications to maintain a clear and accessible architectural record.

Qualifications

Required

  • 9+ years of experience in data architecture, data engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and governing enterprise data lakes or large-scale data platforms.
  • Deep hands-on expertise with Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse Analytics (dedicated sql pool and serverless).
  • Strong experience with data modeling (relational, dimensional, and NoSQL data models).
  • Proven ability to establish and drive data governance programs including metadata management, master data management, data quality, and lineage.
  • Experience collaborating with security and infrastructure teams to implement compliant, secure data architectures.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to present complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

  • Experience with Azure Purview or a similar enterprise data catalog / governance platform
  • Familiarity with Delta Lake, Apache Spark, or similar open-source data processing frameworks within a cloud environment. Familiarity with Azure Data Lake Storage, various database platforms (Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, Postgres, Cosmos), Fabric, Azure Service Bus, Event Hubs, and Logic Apps
  • Exposure to application acquisition and data integration onboarding processes
  • Knowledge of data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA) and their architectural implications.
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Engineer Associate, Azure Solutions Architect Expert or related Azure certification.

Experience in a multi-project or program environment with competing priorities.

TerraPower is seeking a highly talented and motivated candidate for the position of Director, Insurance and Enterprise Risk Management. Director, Insurance and Enterprise Risk Management will report to Associate General Counsel, Legal. TerraPower’s Director, Insurance and Enterprise Risk Management, is responsible for proactively managing TerraPower’s company insurance programs, managing and advising on project-specific insurance, and ensuring that TerraPower responsibly manages business risk through effective claims prevention and management.

Responsibilities

Insurance Program Management:

  • Manage TerraPower’s corporate and project-specific lines of insurance, including corporate property and casualty, financial and professional liability, project-specific insurance placements (e.g., builder’s risk; OCIP/CCIP), and other lines of coverage.
  • Partner with finance to manage TerraPower’s surety program, including bonding capacity, surety relationships, collateral requirements, and indemnity obligations.
  • Function as a subject matter expert on US and international nuclear liability frameworks and nuclear insurance policies. Provide expert guidance on US nuclear licensing requirements, including but not limited to 10 CFR § 50.54(w), 10 CFR § 50.75, and 10 CFR § 140.11.
  • Manage insurance broker relationships and partner with TerraPower’s insurance broker to develop placement strategies, negotiate coverage terms, manage claims, and issue certificates of insurance.
  • Work collaboratively with TerraPower engineering teams and environmental health, and safety (EHS) stakeholders to evaluate and implement loss control measures, with particular consideration for total cost of risk (TCOR).
  • Evaluate, develop, and/or implement alternative risk transfer programs and/or specialty insurance products as needed.
  • Provide continuous analysis of TerraPower risk appetite, risk bearing capacity, and risk sharing standards during insurance placements and renewals, referencing advanced risk analytics and loss modeling, when available.
  • Collaborate with legal, procurement, and contracts teams to negotiate vendor, customer, and other commercial contracts, including indemnity provisions, risk of loss provisions, TerraPower insurance requirements (e.g., policy coverage, limits, and exclusions), and counterparty insurance requirements. Work with contracts and procurement to ensure counterparty compliance with contractual insurance provisions.
  • Ensure TerraPower administers its lines of insurance in accordance with applicable policy terms, conditions, and claims reporting requirements. Review insurance binders, policies, and endorsements to ensure accuracy and inclusion of negotiated terms and conditions.

Enterprise Risk Management (ERM):

  • Manage the taxonomy and governance of the ERM program, including development of scalable processes to identify, assess, mitigate, report, and monitor risks to TerraPower’s strategic goals and company objectives.
  • Oversee annual enterprise risk assessments, including interviews with technical and corporate leadership, to identify emerging risks, validate or recalibrate previously identified risks, and inform enterprise risk reporting and prioritization.
  • Develop and refine enterprise risk appetite and tolerances.
  • Provide executive reports on the ERM program to the ERMC Committee (ERMC) and Board Audit Committee.

General:

Program Ownership and Governance

  • Owns and governs the station’s Engineering programs, including standards, policies, procedures, resource allocation, staffing models, and regulatory compliance.

Operational and Resource Management

  • Develop and manages budgets and long-range resource plans for engineering programs, including personnel, equipment, and facilities.
  • Owns performance monitoring, self-assessment, and corrective action programs for engineering functions.

Regulatory Compliance and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Minimum 10 years of experience at a nuclear power plant
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in management or senior technical leadership roles.

  • Advanced degree in a relevant technical discipline.
  • Professional Engineer Certification
  • Previously held a SRO License or SRO Certification
  • Experience governing engineering programs in Nuclear.

description:
TerraPower is seeking a Director of International Business Development to lead the identification, development, and advancement of international market opportunities for the Natrium reactor and energy system. This individual will report to the Senior Vice President, Business Development and Strategy, and will be a key driver of TerraPower's global growth strategy. They will be charged with building relationships withutilities, industrial partners, financial institutions, and large load customers at all levels, and translating those relationships into structured commercial pathways toward deployment.

This is a high-visibility role requiring a rare combination of team leadership, high-level business development instincts, advanced financial and commercial structuring expertise, and cross-cultural fluency. The ideal candidate can navigate complex government and regulatory environments, structure bankable project frameworks, and build long-term trust with international partners in a highly technical, capital-intensive industry.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • This role is responsible for backing up the SVP of Business Development as needed in critical internal and external business efforts.
  • As function grows, this role may be tasked with building, developing and retaining critical international business development professionals.

Market Development & Strategy

  • Identify, prioritize, and develop international markets for Natrium deployment based on energy policy, demand growth, regulatory readiness, and strategic fit
  • Build and maintain relationships with national utilities, state-owned enterprises, and industrial off-takers
  • Independently represent TerraPower at international conferences, government meetings, trade missions, and industry forums
  • Monitor geopolitical, regulatory, and competitive developments affecting international nuclear markets

Commercial & Financial Structuring

  • Lead the structuring of commercial frameworks for international projects, including EPC arrangements, ownership models, offtake agreements, and risk allocation structures
  • Work closely with TerraPower departments to develop financing strategies incorporating export credit agencies (e.g., EXIM, USTDA), multilateral development banks, sovereign guarantees, and private capital
  • Support development of bankable project economics and term sheets in coordination with business, legal, finance, engineering and other teams
  • Structure and negotiate MOUs, teaming agreements, joint development agreements, and early-stage commercial contracts

Deployment Pathway Management

  • Serve as the internal and external point of coordination driving international opportunities from early engagement through feasibility, site selection, licensing pathway alignment, and toward final investment decision
  • Coordinate cross-functionally with engineering, licensing, supply chain, government affairs, and legal teams to ensure market-specific requirements are reflected in deployment planning
  • Develop and track opportunity pipelines, market entry plans, and business cases for executive leadership and board reporting

Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Cultivate strategic relationships with local partners, EPC firms, utilities, and financial institutions to support market entry and project development

Document Control Analyst

The Document Control Analyst is an intermediate-level position within TerraPower’s Records Management and Document Control (RMDC) program, reporting directly to the RMDC Manager. This role is well-suited for individuals with prior experience in document control or records management in a regulated industry, particularly nuclear. The Analyst supports the full document lifecycle using electronic systems and standard processes, including EPC and construction document control activities, while also contributing to the improvement of RMDC practices, user training, and regulatory readiness. This position requires a high level of attention to detail, the ability to work independently, and a working knowledge of quality and regulatory requirements in the nuclear industry. This is an on-site role based in Kemmerer, WY.

Responsibilities:

  • Support EPC and construction document control processes, including intake, validation, and release of drawings, specifications, RFIs, field changes, and other construction records.
  • Coordinate with site construction, engineering, and EPC teams to ensure timely distribution and access to current‑revision documents in the field.
  • Monitor and help maintain construction document registers, turnover packages, and related metadata to ensure configuration control and traceability across design and construction phases.
  • Administer and maintain TerraPower’s Electronic Document Management System (EDMS), ensuring compliance with document lifecycle requirements including version control, approvals, metadata standards, and archival.
  • Review, edit, and process-controlled documents and Change Orders, verifying alignment with TerraPower procedures and nuclear regulatory expectations.
  • Act as a point of contact for document control support across engineering, quality, licensing, project management, and supply chain functions.
  • Guide internal teams through EDMS workflows, ensuring timely routing, review, and release of documentation.
  • Train TerraPower staff and contractors on RMDC policies, procedures, and EDMS use; assist in onboarding new users.
  • Support records retention, retrieval, and disposition processes consistent with internal schedules and external compliance obligations (e.g., ASME NQA-1, NRC guidance, NIRMA).
  • Perform document audits and quality checks to ensure completeness, accuracy, and regulatory compliance.
  • Help develop and maintain RMDC tools, templates, training materials, and standard work instructions.

They are responsible for the coordination of multiple cross-functional teams needed to complete all aspects of delivery scope throughout the equipment delivery lifecycle. These teams include design engineering, procurement, QA, fabrication, testing, logistics, start-up/commissioning, construction and licensing teams. They are responsible for communication of information to key project stakeholders while ensuring that information is properly controlled.

Tasks

  • Define and lead execution strategy for equipment across multiple teams, functions, and organizations.
  • Articulate requirements, goals, and milestones for equipment delivery with appropriate stakeholders responsible for specific areas (system leads, senior managers, project managers).
  • Drive equipment delivery on time and on budget per the Natrium Project plan.
  • Work with project teams to develop plans, influence teams to deliver to them, and keep leadership informed on progress.
  • Coordinate the timely review of deliverables across cross functional teams.
  • Work with project teams to ensure that work focuses on the highest priority as appropriately reflected in the schedule.
  • Initiate and rapidly execute recovery efforts when cost and schedule items arise.
  • Escalate challenges promptly to ensure they receive adequate attention and resources for resolution.

  • Oversees vendor performance for vendor awarded scope.
  • Monitor contract budgets and approved values to verify that work is adequately funded and aligns with project financial parameters.

  • Manage risks to schedule and budget associated with testing programs.
  • Reinforce organizational accountability for testing programs and results.
  • Facilitate timely incorporation of any test results impacting design.
  • Work with Natrium Fabrication Oversight to manage fabrication vendors, to identify and manage witness or hold point notifications to ensure appropriate stakeholder involvement at critical stages.
  • Work with Natrium Construction team to ensure on-site requirements and strategies for assembly, installation and inspections are integrated with equipment delivery plans.
  • Work with TerraPower QA and Licensing groups to ensure adherence to quality requirements, regulatory guidelines, and industry standards as specified in equipment delivery efforts and documents.

  • Implement accountability and governance checkpoints for testing programs, ensuring compliance with quality standards and timely integration of results into design and delivery plans.
  • Conduct regular prioritization and triage reviews to confirm that work efforts remain focused on the highest-value activities aligned with schedule and risk mitigation.
  • Lead development and implementation of recovery and get-well plans when deviations from cost or schedule occur, ensuring alignment with project objectives.
  • Establish and execute formal escalation management protocols, including triggers, escalation paths, and timing to ensure timely resolution of critical issues.

Key Qualifications and Skills

  • Minimum of 10 years of experience related to Supply Chain, Project Management, or Project Delivery.
  • Proven leader, with a strong technical background, in one or many areas of the scope.
  • Proficient in project management tools such as Jira and P6 (Primavera).
  • Strong familiarity with nuclear codes, standards, and regulations, including ASME BPVC, ASME QME-1, NQA-1, IEEE standards, and industry requirements.

  • Demonstrated experience leading a large project scope across multiple teams with strong dependencies.

  • Thrive and succeed in a fast-paced and changing environment where plans need to adjustment to meet project goals.
  • Strong conflict resolution skills.
  • Creative, proactive, attentive to detail, and can take ownership of problems and their resolution.
  • The successful candidate will possess a high degree of trust and integrity, communicate openly and display respect and a desire to foster teamwork.

Fuel Fabrication Licensing and Criticality Engineer

TerraPower is seeking a Fuel Fabrication Licensing and Criticality Engineer to join the Natrium Fuel Design and Supply team. The Fuel Fabrication Licensing and Criticality Engineer is responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining nuclear criticality safety analyses and controls supporting the fabrication of Natrium fuel. The Fuel Fabrication Licensing and Criticality Engineer will integrate criticality safety into facility and process design and will be involved with process development, production readiness, technical documentation, and supplier coordination. This role requires quality-driven execution for safety critical components and fabrication processes.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop nuclear criticality safety evaluations for fuel fabrication process steps, fresh fuel receipt, storage, handling, inspection, and transportation operations.
  • Perform criticality safety calculations using industry-standard computational tools (i.e. SCALE/KENO, MCNP, etc) for Natrium fuel fabrication and related processes, including areas related to HALEU feedstock, fuel fabrication, and fresh fuel storage and transportation.
  • Establish engineered and administrative controls to ensure subcriticality under normal, abnormal, and credible accident conditions.
  • Develop and maintain Criticality Safety Evaluations, Criticality Safety Limits, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Support design reviews to ensure equipment, storage configurations, fuel fabrication processes, and facility layouts satisfy criticality safety requirements.
  • Evaluate design changes through engineering change processes and assess impacts to nuclear criticality safety.
  • Support licensing activities by preparing technical reports, regulatory responses, and safety analyses for NRC review.
  • Interface with fuel vendors and transportation organizations to support packaging, shipping, and receipt of fresh HALEU fuel.
  • Support development of operating procedures, training materials, and operational readiness reviews.
  • Participate in hazard analyses, design reviews, audits, and independent technical assessments.
  • Support development of criticality safety programs consistent with ANSI/ANS-8 standards and applicable NRC regulations.
  • Support continuous learning and application of nuclear industry best practices to maintain the highest quality of engineering design and proactively identify process change/enhancement opportunities.

Key Qualifications and Skills

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Nuclear Engineering or closely related engineering discipline.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in nuclear criticality safety, reactor physics, fuel cycle engineering, or a related nuclear engineering field.
  • Experience performing criticality safety analyses using Monte Carlo neutron transport methods.
  • Working knowledge of nuclear cross-section libraries and uncertainty methodologies.
  • Familiarity with NRC regulations applicable to criticality safety and fuel handling.
  • Experience preparing technical reports and engineering calculations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Ability to work with minimum direction to solve challenging problems.
  • Ability to work on multiple tasks concurrently during a given work week.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • The successful candidate will possess a high degree of trust and integrity, communicate openly, and display respect and a desire to foster teamwork.

The Ideal Candidate:

  • Experience supporting advanced reactors, sodium-cooled fast reactors, or fuel cycle facilities.
  • Experience with HALEU fuel systems.
  • Experience with fast-spectrum criticality methodology.
  • Proficiency with SCALE, MCNP, Serpent, or comparable neutron transport software.
  • Familiarity with ANSI/ANS-8 criticality safety standards.
  • Experience with nuclear industry manufacturing and operation, DOE and NRC regulations
  • Experience with NQA-1 / QL-1 standards or other highly controlled production standards
  • Strong understanding of nuclear safety culture.

Loop Engineer - Test and Fill Facility

The Loop Engineer will be responsible for the configuration, operation, and performance of sodium test loops supporting Natrium development and validation activities. This role focuses on high-temperature liquid sodium systems and associated inserting, fill, drain, purification, and thermal-hydraulic test capabilities at TerraPower’s test facilities.

As a member of the Test and Fill Facility team the engineer will work closely with, Natrium system engineers, safety analysis, operations and maintenance staff to ensure sodium loop tests are planned and executed safely, efficiently, and with high data quality.

Key Responsibilities

  • Refine sodium test loop configurations to represent Natrium operating conditions (flow, temperature, pressure, transients, and chemistry).
  • Support P&ID development, equipment layout, and integration with facility utilities (power, inert gas, ventilation, fire protection, and safety systems).
  • Perform steady-state and transient system analyses of sodium loops to define operating envelopes, setpoints, and test conditions.
  • Calculate pressure drops, flow distribution, thermal profiles, and equipment performance margins based on loop configuration and test objectives.
  • Support test matrix development, including definition of key parameters (flow, temperature, thermal cycling, upset conditions) and required measurement accuracy.
  • Develop and maintain operating procedures, start-up and shutdown sequences, and abnormal event response for sodium loops.
  • Provide engineering support to operations during test runs, including real-time assessment of loop performance and troubleshooting.
  • Monitor loop parameters (sodium temperature, flow, level, pressure, oxygen/hydrogen content, cover gas conditions) for compliance with test plans and facility limits.
  • Diagnose and resolve performance issues related to pumps, heaters, valves, instrumentation, and control logic in sodium service.
  • Ensure sodium loop designs and operations comply with facility safety bases, hazard analyses, and applicable codes/standards.
  • Support and/or perform hazard analyses, FMEA, and operating limit definition for sodium systems (e.g., leak scenarios, freeze/melt, over-temperature).
  • Maintain configuration control of loop hardware, and software, including documentation of changes and formal review/approval processes.
  • Contribute to development and maintenance of emergency procedures for sodium-related events and abnormal loop conditions.
  • Define instrumentation needs for sodium loops (thermocouples, flow meters, pressure transducers, level sensors, chemistry probes, and cover gas measurements), including ranges, accuracies, and locations.
  • Collaborate with data acquisition and controls staff to ensure reliable, time-synchronized data collection and appropriate sampling rates for transients.
  • Validate and interpret test data, comparing results with analytical models and design expectations; identify discrepancies and support root cause investigations.
  • Prepare concise technical reports and presentations translating loop results into actionable input for Natrium systems, safety analysis, and design teams.
  • Support vendor interactions for sodium-compatible equipment, defining test requirements and integration approaches.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Chemical, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline
  • Typically 3–8 years of relevant experience in thermal-hydraulic systems, test facilities, nuclear/industrial process systems, or high-temperature fluid loops.
  • Strong understanding of fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and thermodynamics, with practical application to loop design and operation.

description:
The TerraPower Isotopes® (TPI™) division has been established to pursue medical isotopes development--advancing nuclear science for significant human health benefits. We seek to support revolutionary radiotherapies for treatments of various cancers through the supply of radioisotopes. TerraPower currently has unique access to a supply of thorium for the long-term production of actinium-225 in the growing alpha therapy market and intends to expand into other nuclear related medical treatments.

The TerraPower Isotopes program is an integral part of the Washington State based TerraPower team, a company working to raise living standards globally. In 2006, the company originated with Bill Gates and a group of like-minded visionaries who evaluated the fundamental challenges to raising living standards around the world. TerraPower’s mission is to be a world leader in new nuclear technologies, while developing innovators and future leaders in the nuclear field.

TPI is seeking to hire highly motivated and forward-thinking professionals who are interested in focusing on advanced radiopharmaceutical applications and influencing change within nuclear medicine. TerraPower is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Manager, Operations Programs

The TerraPower Isotopes (TPI) Manager, Operations Programs reports to the Director of Operations and is responsible for establishing, leading, and continuously improving the programs and management systems that support safe, reliable, and high-performing operations teams. This role will lead the development of scalable systems; hire, manage, and develop the program leaders responsible for those systems; and lead key cross-functional initiatives important to the growth of the larger TPI organization.

A central responsibility of this role is to build leadership capability within Operations as the organization grows. The Core Operations Program Manager will coach technically capable program leaders to progress from ownership of individual programs toward broader cross-functional leadership and, as organizational needs and individual capabilities develop, leadership of operational teams. The role will help establish a pipeline of future Operations leaders capable of assuming increasing responsibility as TPI scales.

Responsibilities:

Operations Program Leadership

  • Own the development, governance, implementation, performance, and continuous improvement of assigned TPI Operations programs, including Training & Qualification, Documentation & Process Management, Operations Performance Improvement, and Compliance.
  • Establish scalable program frameworks, standards, governance, and management processes that support reliable production, organizational growth, and increasing cGMP maturity.
  • Establish measures of program effectiveness and ensure assigned programs are effectively implemented, sustained, evaluated, and improved as operational needs evolve.

Leadership & Development

  • Hire, manage, coach, and develop Program Administrators responsible for assigned Operations programs, establishing clear priorities, expectations, accountability, and appropriate decision-making authority.
  • Coach and develop team members from strong individual program owners into broader organizational leaders through coaching, feedback, mentoring, delegation, and progressively challenging cross-functional and people-leadership assignments.
  • Build a leadership pipeline capable of assuming increasing responsibility for programs, projects, and operational teams as TPI grows, while fostering a culture of ownership, accountability, technical rigor, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

Cross-Functional Technical Leadership

  • Lead selected complex, non-routine, and strategically important Operations initiatives from problem definition and planning through implementation and sustained execution.
  • Lead and influence cross-functional teams to resolve technical and operational interfaces, dependencies, competing priorities, and assigned actions.
  • Rapidly develop sufficient understanding of complex technical issues to ask effective questions, challenge assumptions, integrate subject-matter expertise, and translate technical and operational needs into executable programs and decisions.

Operations Strategy & Management

  • Partner with Operations leadership to establish program priorities aligned with production objectives, organizational growth, regulatory requirements, and business needs.
  • Advise the Director of Operations on program performance, organizational and technical risks, resource requirements, emerging needs, and recommended priorities, and provide program information to other TPI leaders as required.
  • Anticipate program and organizational needs as TPI grows and recommend improvements to systems, resources, responsibilities, and organizational capabilities.

Master’s degree in engineering, business administration, or a related technical or management field preferred.
  • Minimum 8 years of experience working in the nuclear or other industry under an established radiation protection program and under a regulated framework.
  • Demonstrated technical aptitude and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to rapidly understand complex scientific, engineering, and operational issues and effectively engage technical subject-matter experts.
  • Demonstrated success managing, coaching, and developing professional employees, including developing high-potential individuals toward increasing levels of organizational, people, and operational leadership.
  • Strong people leadership skills, including the ability to recognize individual strengths and development needs, delegate meaningful responsibility, provide candid feedback, establish accountability, and develop independent leaders rather than dependent followers.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives involving multiple technical disciplines, stakeholders, and competing priorities, including leadership through influence without direct authority.
  • Experience building or scaling teams, program-management functions, operations organizations, or leadership capability in a growing or changing environment.
  • PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or comparable program-management or process-improvement training or certification is a plus.
  • Familiarity with artificial intelligence tools and their effective application to program management, information systems, or business processes is a plus.
  • Military leadership or technical operations experience is a plus.
  • Ability to work flexible hours as operational and business needs require.

The successful candidate will combine strong organizational and program-management capability with high technical aptitude, intellectual curiosity, and demonstrated people leadership. Manager, R&D Radiochemistry

The Manager of Radiochemical Process Development, R&D Radiochemistry reports to the Director, R&D Radiochemistry, and is responsible for managing the TPI R&D Radiochemistry Process Development team members in their efforts to develop, scale‑up, and support operation of chemical processes for the long-term production of actinium‑225.

The position will exercise significant judgement in ensuring TPI maintains regulatory compliance while delivering on commercial production and engineering design needs. description:
The TerraPower Isotopes® (TPI™) division has been established to pursue medical isotopes development--advancing nuclear science for significant human health benefits. We seek to support revolutionary radiotherapies for treatments of various cancers through the supply of radioisotopes. TerraPower currently has unique access to a supply of thorium for the long-term production of actinium-225 in the growing alpha therapy market and intends to expand into other nuclear related medical treatments.

The TerraPower Isotopes program is an integral part of the Washington State based TerraPower team, a company working to raise living standards globally. In 2006, the company originated with Bill Gates and a group of like-minded visionaries who evaluated the fundamental challenges to raising living standards around the world. TerraPower’s mission is to be a world leader in new nuclear technologies, while developing innovators and future leaders in the nuclear field.

TPI is seeking to hire highly motivated and forward-thinking professionals who are interested in focusing on advanced radiopharmaceutical applications and influencing change within nuclear medicine. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Performance Improvement Administrator

The Performance Improvement Administrator reports to the Operations Program Manager and is responsible for administering and advancing performance-improvement activities across TPI Operations. The position leads significant investigations and causal analyses, coordinates corrective actions and operational changes, manages issue and lessons-learned processes, and conducts audits and surveillances to strengthen performance and prevent recurrence.

The Performance Improvement Administrator works with Operations management, Quality, Engineering, R&D, and other technical organizations to evaluate events, adverse conditions, trends, and improvement opportunities. The position supports applicable cGMP quality and change processes and administers a structured performance-improvement framework for non-GMP Operations work using methods proportionate to significance and risk.

This position operates in a dynamic, interdisciplinary, and highly technical environment in which sound judgment, analytical rigor, effective communication, influence without direct authority, and the ability to constructively challenge existing practices are required.

Responsibilities:

Investigations and Corrective Actions

  • Lead significant Operations investigations, post-event critiques, after-action reviews, and root cause analyses; establish the appropriate scope and provide guidance for lower-level reviews.
  • Collect and evaluate evidence, records, interviews, and timelines to establish facts, identify causal factors, and assess the extent of identified conditions.
  • Prepare clear and defensible investigation reports and facilitate corrective and preventive actions that address identified causes and are practical to implement.
  • Review causal analyses and corrective actions for adequacy, track implementation and effectiveness, and elevate overdue or ineffective actions.

Change and Issue Management

  • Coordinate the Operations change-control process from initiation through closure, including scope definition, stakeholder coordination, impact evaluation, implementation planning, and action tracking.
  • Administer the Operations issue log, including intake, screening, classification, assignment, status tracking, closure verification, and reporting.
  • Recommend responses to operational issues based on significance and risk, maintain visibility of open items, and elevate emerging concerns to responsible managers.

Audits, Surveillances, and Operating Discipline

  • Develop and administer an Operations audit and surveillance program addressing procedural compliance, work practices, training and qualification, equipment status, documentation, housekeeping, 5S, and other operational controls.
  • Conduct or coordinate audits, surveillances, field observations, and management assessments; document results; and track required follow-up.
  • Promote procedural compliance, effective pre-job briefs and post-job reviews, formality of operations, and consistent standards during production activities, and communicate declining performance or recurring weaknesses to Operations management.

Trending, Lessons Learned, and Program Improvement

  • Analyze events, issues, findings, corrective actions, and other performance information to identify recurring causes, adverse trends, and emerging risks, and prepare routine reports for Operations management.
  • Maintain internal and external lessons learned, evaluate applicability to TPI Operations, and coordinate incorporation into procedures, training, pre-evolution briefs, and other work controls.
  • Lead or support structured improvement initiatives and coach Operations personnel and managers in investigation, causal analysis, corrective-action development, operating discipline, and performance-improvement methods.

Key Qualifications & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, quality, business, operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Five or more years of relevant experience in operations, quality, engineering, investigations, performance improvement, regulated manufacturing, military operations, or a related function.
  • Experience in a regulated, quality-controlled, or similarly structured environment is preferred. Nuclear, pharmaceutical, radiopharmaceutical, or cGMP experience is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead event investigations, post-event critiques, causal analyses, and corrective-action development.
  • Formal training or certification in root cause analysis, event investigation, Lean Six Sigma, or a comparable performance-improvement methodology is preferred. Experience implementing 5S or similar workplace-organization practices is a plus.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to establish facts, identify causal factors, evaluate the extent and significance of issues, recognize adverse trends, and develop practical recommendations.
  • Strong technical writing skills with demonstrated ability to prepare clear, objective, and defensible investigation reports, assessments, corrective-action documentation, and management presentations.
  • Experience administering structured performance-improvement processes, including change control, issue management, audits and surveillances, corrective actions, or lessons learned.
  • Strong facilitation and interpersonal skills with the ability to lead difficult discussions, constructively challenge assumptions, coach personnel and managers, and influence without direct authority.
  • Strong organizational skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple investigations and actions through completion, work independently, exercise sound judgment, and appropriately handle sensitive information.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office and SharePoint. Experience with Jira, quality-management systems, or reporting tools is preferred.
  • Military nuclear, maintenance, training, quality, or operational experience is a plus.

Principal Engineer, Safety Methods

This role supports the development, enhancement, and deployment of plant‑scale thermal‑hydraulic analysis methods and models for the Natrium reactor. Reporting to the Manager, Plant Thermal Hydraulics Methods, the principal engineer supports the creation, improvement and qualification of advanced system-level modeling approaches that enable accurate, robust prediction of plant behavior across operational and transient scenarios.

The position requires expertise in system‑level thermal‑hydraulics, thermal‑fluids behavior, computational methods, and scaling analysis supporting benchmarking computational models against experimental data.

Responsibilities

  • Support verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification activities for plant scale thermal-hydraulic analysis tools.
  • Develop and execute code assessment plans, including validation matrices, test selection, and quantitative comparison methodologies.
  • Perform scaling analysis to evaluate the applicability of test data to reference system conditions, including assessment of similarity criteria and scaling distortion.
  • Interpret and apply experimental data from separate effects and integral test facilities to support model validation and closure of technical gaps.
  • Define validation needs, develop test requirements, and collaborate closely with test engineering teams to ensure alignment between model gaps and experimental programs.
  • Document V&V methodologies, model assumptions, validation results, and uncertainty analyses for internal design processes and regulatory submittals.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to support plant design, safety analysis, and licensing workflows.
  • Apply and improve TerraPower’s SQA and NQA1 modeling quality practices and ensure traceability and configuration control of analysis inputs, models, and results.
  • Mentor junior engineers in system modeling, validation methodologies, and best practices in code assessment.

Key Qualifications and Skills

  • Degree in Mechanical, Nuclear, Chemical Engineering, or similar field, with 8 plus years in the field of system‑level thermal‑hydraulic analysis and code assessment for nuclear or complex energy systems.
  • Demonstrated experience in code assessment, including model-to-test comparison, validation metric development, and uncertainty quantification.
  • Hands‑on experience working with experimental thermal‑hydraulic data, including data analysis, uncertainty evaluation, and comparison against system‑level predictions.
  • Proficiency with system analysis tools (e.g., RELAP5‑3D, TRACE, SAS, or equivalent) applied to plant‑scale transient and steady-state evaluations.
  • Strong foundation in thermal-fluid and reactor system behavior considerations relevant to advanced reactor designs.
  • Experience performing scaling analysis to ensure appropriate translation test-scale phenomena, including application of similarity criteria and detailed scaling distortion impact qualifications.
  • Experience developing validation strategies, defining data needs, and coordinating with experimental programs.

Principal Nuclear Licensing Engineer

Terrapower is seeking an experienced and strategic Principal Nuclear Licensing Engineer to join the Regulatory Affairs and Licensing team. Reporting to the Sr. VP of Regulatory Affairs, this leader will provide advanced licensing expertise, influence regulatory strategy, mentor licensing staff, and drive high‑impact licensing activities for the Natrium advanced reactor project. The role includes leading development of licensing documents, directing regulatory interactions, and ensuring that licensing approaches are fully aligned with TerraPower’s long‑term regulatory strategy.

This position requires deep proficiency in U.S. NRC regulations and guidance, extensive experience preparing and reviewing licensing applications, and a demonstrated ability to lead complex regulatory engagements. The Principal Nuclear Licensing Engineer will collaborate closely with engineering, project management, partners, and contractors to ensure successful, timely, and compliant licensing outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Lead development, authorship, and technical review of complex licensing documents, including major sections of an Operating License Application (e.g., Safety Analysis Report, Environmental Report).
  • Provide strategic direction for regulatory engagement plans, technical justifications, and licensing pathways to support project goals.
  • Coordinate multi‑disciplinary teams to prepare high‑quality responses to NRC audit questions and requests for additional information.
  • Mentor junior and mid‑level licensing engineers; provide guidance on regulatory interpretation, drafting approaches, and NRC engagement.
  • Serve as a senior interface with the Licensing Team to scope, prioritize, and execute licensing activities.
  • Collaborate with design and engineering teams to ensure regulatory compliance in design development, modifications, and configuration control.
  • Oversee preparation, review, and control of licensing documentation in accordance with regulatory requirements and stringent QA standards.
  • Lead technical and strategic interactions with partners, contractors, and internal engineering disciplines.
  • Review and provide final approval recommendations on correspondence to and from regulatory agencies.
  • Contribute significantly to the development of TerraPower’s licensing strategy, ensuring alignment with project timelines, risk profiles, and regulatory guidance.

We seek to support revolutionary radiotherapies for treatments of various cancers through the supply of radioisotopes. TerraPower currently has unique access to a supply of thorium for the long-term production of actinium-225 in the growing alpha therapy market and intends to expand into other nuclear related medical treatments.

The TerraPower Isotopes program is an integral part of the Washington State based TerraPower team, a company working to raise living standards globally. Project Manager

TerraPower Isotopes® (TPI™) is seeking an experienced Project Manager to work within the TPI Project Office and carry a dual mandate: help build the Project Office itself while directly delivering the project work of TPI’s engineering, technology, and R&D functions. As TPI scales its actinium-225 production capability, this role is central to standing up the frameworks, controls, and tooling that will govern how work is planned, resourced, measured, and delivered across the enterprise—and to putting those frameworks into practice on live scope from day one.

This is a builder’s role for someone who has helped establish a project management office or project controls function inside a fast-moving, high-growth organization and wants to do it again in a mission-driven, highly regulated setting. You will partner with engineering, technology, R&D, and operations leaders to plan and drive their project scope, and you will help architect the governance, project controls, and portfolio disciplines that TPI’s future-state Project Office is built on. Success in this role depends on strong project controls fundamentals, sound judgment, and the ability to operate with limited direction in an environment where priorities move quickly and regulatory rigor is non-negotiable.

TPI intends to fill more than one position from this posting, spanning general project delivery, project controls and scheduling, and portfolio reporting and analytics. Actual position starting level, focus area, and title will be determined based on assessment of qualifications.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the embedded project manager for one or more engineering and technology functions (for example Systems Engineering, mechanical and containment design, process integration, or R&D chemistry), planning and driving the delivery of their project scope end to end.
  • Contribute to the design and stand-up of the TPI Project Office framework, including governance structures, delivery-lane definitions, and the cross-cutting disciplines of project controls, risk management, vendor and contract management, and portfolio management.
  • Build and maintain project controls across assigned scope: develop work breakdown structures from the ground up, establish resource-loaded schedules, and manage baselines throughout execution.
  • Coordinate scheduling in Primavera P6 with the master scheduler, including resource loading and leveling, integration of external engineering and vendor schedules, and the recurring update and reporting cycle.
  • Establish and run performance measurement and reporting, including milestone and earned-value tracking, variance analysis, and a clear reporting cadence—including portfolio dashboards (for example Power BI)—for project teams and leadership.
  • Operate change management through a disciplined project change request process, maintaining live change logs and risk registers and driving timely resolution.
  • Support portfolio intake and categorization, ensuring new and in-flight work is classified consistently and planned to an appropriate level of fidelity.
  • Stand up and steward project management tooling—including enterprise scheduling, time tracking, and portfolio reporting—with attention to keeping validated-quality systems and project tooling appropriately separated.
  • Coordinate interfaces with contracted engineering and EPC partners and with specialized equipment vendors, holding scope, schedule, and deliverable expectations to agreed standards.
  • Author and refine Project Office governance artifacts—policies, procedures, and templates—and support the training and adoption that make them stick across the organization.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with quality, operations, engineering, and R&D to keep delivery aligned with safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements.

Key Qualifications and Skills

  • B.S. in Engineering, Chemistry, Physics or a related discipline from an accredited university, and 6+ years of project management experience with a strong foundation in project controls (scheduling, cost, earned value, and change control).
  • Demonstrated experience helping build or stand up a project management office, project controls function, or comparable delivery framework—ideally within a startup, scale-up, or other fast-growth environment.

  • Experience delivering projects in a regulated or high-compliance environment such as cGMP/pharmaceutical, nuclear, aerospace, or other safety-critical industry.

The Quality Control Microbiologist will establish, implement, and execute microbiological testing programs supporting radiopharmaceutical manufacturing in compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), FDA and ICH guidance, EU Annex 1, biosafety standards, and radiation safety requirements.

This role will develop laboratory capabilities, perform routine and specialized microbiological testing, support contamination control initiatives, and serve as a microbiology subject matter expert (SME) during audits and cross‑functional projects.

The QC Lead Microbiologist will work closely with Quality Assurance, QC Radiochemistry, R&D, Operations, Engineering, Project Management and Radiation Safety.

This position is ideal for professionals experienced in startup environments who enjoy building systems while maintaining strong hands‑on laboratory presence.

  • Maintain compliant laboratory operations, including media management, equipment calibration, qualification, laboratory data integrity and follow biosafety and radiological safety requirements.
  • Lead or support development and implementation of a comprehensive site-specific CCS in collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Lead risk assessments for contamination sources and recommend mitigation strategies throughout facility design and commissioning.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert (SME) for regulatory audits and internal inspections focused on microbiological controls.
  • Independently assess and troubleshoot complex microbiological issues, proposing and implementing corrective/preventive actions as needed.
  • Train QC and Operations staff in aseptic techniques and microbiology best practices.
  • Build strong working relationships across technical and operational functions.
  • Balance Quality requirements with safety, such as biosafety and radiation safety, in all Quality initiatives.

Receiving & Inventory Specialist

The Receiving & Inventory Specialist for the Test & Fill Facility is responsible for ensuring the accurate receipt, inspection, inventory control, and storage of materials that support Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), operational readiness for the Natrium Test & Fill Facility. This role ensures that materials are available, correctly documented, and properly stored to meet quality, safety, and schedule requirements for the Natrium program.

The successful candidate will establish and maintain robust receiving and inventory processes, coordinate closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, Engineering, and EHS to maintain robust material control, support SAT execution, and uphold TerraPower’s standards for nuclear-related and safety-significant components for a first-of-a-kind Test & Fill Facility.

Key Responsibilities

Receiving & Receipt Inspection

  • Receive, verify, and log all incoming materials against POs and packing lists.
  • Perform receipt inspections to defined criteria; verify certifications, documentation, and part identification.
  • Identify, document, and segregate nonconforming or damaged materials; coordinate returns and dispositions.

Inventory Control & Material Staging

  • Maintain accurate, real-time inventory records in TerraPower systems, including traceability data where required.
  • Perform cycle counts and reconcile discrepancies; support audits of inventory accuracy.
  • Stage and kit materials for Test & Fill operations and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) in alignment with schedules and work orders.
  • Coordinate availability, staging, and timely issue of materials, components, and consumables for SAT activities.
  • Ensure that materials used in SAT are properly received, inspected, traceable, and documented.
  • Capture and file material-related SAT records (e.g., as-used lists, certificates, inspection reports) to support configuration management.

Storage, Handling & Preservation

  • Implement proper storage, labeling, and status identification to protect material integrity and prevent unintended use.
  • Apply special storage and handling requirements (environmental controls, segregation, hazardous materials handling) per procedures and supplier/engineering requirements.
  • Monitor shelf life and condition of stored materials; coordinate replacement of expired or compromised items.

Process, Compliance & Collaboration

  • Follow TerraPower EHS, quality, and material control procedures; support internal and external audits.
  • Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, QA, EHS, and Supply Chain to plan material needs and resolve issues.
  • Contribute to improvements in receiving, inspection, inventory, and storage processes and tools.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience in receiving, inventory control, warehouse operations, or logistics in an industrial, manufacturing, or technical environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform detailed receipt inspections and maintain accurate records and documentation.
  • Familiarity with inventory management systems or ERP platforms, and proficiency with common office software (e.g., spreadsheets, databases, word processing).
  • Ability to read and interpret basic technical documentation (purchase orders, packing lists, datasheets, drawings, and specifications).
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Effective communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with operations, engineering, QA, and EHS personnel.
  • Ability to safely lift and move materials and to operate material handling equipment (e.g., pallet jacks, forklifts) after appropriate training and certification.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a highly regulated environment such as nuclear, aerospace, defense, or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
  • Working knowledge of quality assurance principles, material traceability, and configuration control; familiarity with NQA-1 or similar quality frameworks is a plus.
  • Experience supporting test facilities, commissioning activities, or Site Acceptance Testing, particularly related to material management and documentation.
  • Experience establishing or refining receiving and inventory processes for new or evolving facilities.

Senior Analytical Chemist

TerraPower, LLC is committed to delivering transformative nuclear technologies that provide safe, cost-effective, and carbon-free energy solutions, supporting global decarbonization goals. The Natrium program is a cornerstone of this effort, and we are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Analytical Chemist to join our team.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the analytical foundation of the Natrium advanced reactor program. As a member of the Natrium Central Chemistry team, you will be directly responsible for advancing the chemical understanding of Natrium systems and processes and for developing robust analytical and experimental capabilities that support the characterization and chemistry control of sodium, solar salt, fuel/material-related samples, cover gas, and other Natrium process streams.

Reporting to the Natrium Central Chemistry Discipline Senior Manager, you will serve as both a technical leader and hands-on contributor, designing experiments, developing robust analytical methodologies, setting up and operating laboratory equipment, analyzing and interpreting experimental data, and providing critical data that underpins reactor safety, materials performance, chemistry control, and operational readiness. The position requires deep technical expertise, strong experimental judgment, and a strong collaborative spirit to interface effectively with colleagues across design, operations, materials, fuel, safety, testing, and safeguards teams.

Responsibilities

  • Lead development and implementation of robust analytical methods and procedures for Natrium sample characterization, including ICP-MS, ICP-OES, gamma spectroscopy where applicable, and other relevant techniques
  • Lead and perform thermophysical and thermal characterization activities using techniques such as DSC and TGA, including experimental planning, data collection, analysis, and interpretation
  • Perform and interpret thermodynamic calculations using FactSage, Thermochimica, or similar tools to support sodium, solar salt, cover gas, fuel/material, and impurity chemistry evaluations
  • Design, set up, execute, and document laboratory experiments supporting Natrium chemistry, materials, and process-development needs
  • Develop experimental approaches to address technical questions involving sodium, salts, cover gas, corrosion products, impurities, materials, and other Natrium-relevant systems
  • Develop, generate, and review the generation and review of technical work products such as certificates of analysis/conformance, research reports, procedures, and publications
  • Manage analytical scope related to measuring purity, and performing mass balance evaluations of Natrium-relevant materials and analysis of in-process samples for quality control
  • Lead the development and implementation of robust chemical and analytical separation processes needed to produce high quality data from high-salt-matrix and other challenging Natrium samples
  • Lead and support installation, calibration, maintenance, and troubleshooting of Natrium analytical instruments and equipment
  • Take ownership of laboratory equipment and experimental systems, including development of operating procedures, maintenance strategies, calibration requirements, and troubleshooting
  • Analyze experimental data, evaluate data quality and uncertainty, identify trends and anomalies, and translate results into actionable technical conclusions and recommendations for Natrium engineering teams
  • Ensure laboratory procedures are developed, maintained, and continuously improved
  • Maintain high standards of organization, housekeeping, and operational effectiveness in Natrium analytical and chemistry facilities
  • Ensure strict adherence to site safety, chemical safety, and, where applicable, radiation protection and regulatory guidelines, working closely with health physicists, authorized users, and the RSO as required
  • Promote a culture of safety in all experimental and operational activities
  • Drive continuous improvement in analytical capabilities, safety practices, and team effectiveness
  • Perform other general duties associated with position as member of the Natrium Central Chemistry team to ensure ongoing effectiveness and continuous improvement of TerraPower efforts

Key Qualifications:

  • Master’s or Ph.D degree in chemistry, materials science, chemical engineering, physical science, or a related technical field required; (Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience with a Master’s, or a Ph.D.)
  • Experience with thermodynamic modeling using FactSage, Thermochimica, or similar software is desirable
  • Hands-on experience with analytical characterization techniques such as ICP-MS, ICP-OES, gamma spectroscopy, or related elemental/isotopic analytical methods. Expertise in multiple techniques is preferred but experience with every listed technique is not required
  • Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, or other thermophysical/thermal characterization techniques is highly desirable
  • Proven track record in analytical method development using relevant analytical or materials-characterization techniques
  • Demonstrated experience designing, setting up, executing, and troubleshooting laboratory experiments and experimental systems including equipment installation, commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and troubleshooting is highly desirable
  • Experience handling sodium metal or other air- or moisture-sensitive/reactive materials desired
  • Experience working in gloveboxes, inert-atmosphere systems, or controlled-environment experimental systems is desirable
  • Experience with chemical and radiochemical separations (e.g., column separations, liquid-liquid extractions) is desirable
  • Experience with quantitative data analysis, statistical analysis, Python, chemometrics, or machine-learning approaches is desirable
  • Experience with gas chromatography, mass spectrometry, gas analysis, Raman spectroscopy, or other complementary analytical techniques is a plus
  • Experience supporting materials testing, corrosion studies, fuel/material compatibility studies, or high-temperature chemistry experiments is a plus
  • Demonstrated ability to independently plan and execute technical work while collaborating effectively with scientists and engineers from multiple disciplines
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to convey complex technical information clearly to diverse stakeholders
  • Proven ability to work collaboratively, build trust, and foster teamwork across multidisciplinary teams
  • High degree of professional integrity, openness, and respect in interactions with colleagues and external partners

Responsibilities:

  • Select appropriate terms and conditions for procurements and select the right contract vehicle for the need.
  • Review and refine Statements of Work to ensure requirements are clearly written for potential suppliers, with no ambiguity.
  • Lead sourcing and bidding activities, including Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Quotes (RFQs), and Expressions of Interest (EOIs).

  • Negotiate favorable pricing, terms, schedule, and delivery commitments with suppliers.
  • Issue subcontracts, purchase orders, and change orders; monitor and expedite orders to ensure on-time delivery.
  • Ensure all procurement activity fully complies with prime contract requirements and company policy.

  • Solid understanding of federal cost principles.
  • Experience handling export-controlled information.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform job duties with little to no supervision.
  • Comfortably operating in a fast-paced environment with a sizable workload.
  • Highly organized, with strong follow-through and the ability to work collaboratively across teams.
